pairs.why: A's coffin has flat planar lid and walls with tight beveled edges like the real stone slabs, while B is a swollen, soft-cornered pillowy slab.
A's rope is a chunky, compact mass with a tight coil like the solid real objects, whereas B is a thin wire-like lasso with a big open hole and sprawling silhouette.
A has a crisp geometric cone, a flat elliptical brim with a clean edge and a square buckle like the real cap, while B is floppy, drooping and soft-edged.
B's coil is a tighter, bulkier compact mass with a clean round ring, closer to the solid real silhouettes than A's loose, spidery coil with dangling tail.
Both turn the real square-topped rectangular door into an arch with a rounded top, so form gives no reason to prefer either.
B keeps the real chair's armless part count, with thin tube rails and a flat back panel, while A adds arms and chunky padded rests that the real card lacks.
A's thick, stubby barrel and chunky mount match the bulky, fat-barrelled real objects better than B's long thin tapered tube.
A's block pedestal with a flat base plate and plain cylinder stools match the real planar slab and straight-sided stool forms, whereas B uses flared baluster stools and a moulded pedestal.
